title: Cutoff-adaptive threshold-four core rule audit
question: Do the separately certified V=2, d=17, d=18 and d=19 rows admit one predeclared cutoff-adaptive threshold-four core/tail rule, with every coordinate classified by a directed log-ratio interval and no threshold ambiguity?

rule.name: directed-log-ratio-cutoff-adaptive-core
rule.reference_probability: maximum midpoint of the directed row intervals

assumptions: The R-435, R-436 and R-438 primary rows are directed interval authorities for the same V=2, beta=8, right-oriented unconditional ordinal-zero rule.
The maximum midpoint probability is selected only from each already fixed row and is not chosen from the resulting gap or support.
The stored row endpoints have sufficient precision for directed Decimal logarithm classification; every margin is checked against the strict threshold inequalities.
The expected supports in this manifest are test oracles copied from the parent source contracts, not derived claims about a limit.
An adaptive finite support rule may be non-nested and may have non-monotone cardinality; neither property is silently inferred from this audit.
missing_assumptions: An analytic cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform tail modulus for the adaptive supports.
Nested or transported embeddings of the cutoff-dependent cores into one common Q3 domain.
Residual-reuse closure and a common unbounded Hamiltonian core with OS/KMS/GNS identification.
A physical-sector reference, physical-empty comparison and any C6 or Sector-A transfer.
stop_conditions: If a row contract differs across cutoffs, stop and report contract drift.
If any coordinate interval straddles the threshold, classify the rule as ambiguous and do not certify the adaptive support.
If an independent row disagrees with the primary support, fail the control rather than changing the rule.
Never promote a finite adaptive support rule to a uniform tail theorem, physical result, Yang-Mills result or mass-gap statement.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED FINITE CUTOFF-ADAPTIVE SUPPORT-RULE AUDIT; NO UNIFORM OR PHYSICAL PROMOTION
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform tail modulus.
No nested common core, residual-reuse closure, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sector gap.
No physical-empty energy sign, Reading-H stationarity or symmetry-projected transverse stability.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean checks only the finite partition cardinalities and threshold-rule scope; logarithmic interval arithmetic remains executable Python evidence.

boundary: R-439 certifies one deterministic cutoff-adaptive threshold-four classification on the three finite V=2 rows. The supports are not asserted to be nested or uniform, and this result supplies no common-core, physical or Yang-Mills conclusion.
